scope: lib/hvac-permanent.js: transient per-device first-target state and cleanup
lib/hvac-coordination.js: narrow Peak Guard OFF exception for active comfort cycles during charging
behavior: Heating and cooling retain first-target ownership only after successful output
Target reached remains latched if OFF is superseded before publication
Fresh cycle on next eligible start; per-device state and rounded target
PV, tariff, periodic, learning, Flow and external setpoint/mode takeovers clear ownership
No protection from partial or failed starts
Peak Guard does not stop an acknowledged standard comfort session before its first target while charging
No new-start exemption; adequate headroom still permits ordinary starts
Discharging, idle and pending/effective discharge do not get the exception
Stale grid, outdoor OFF, explicit Flow stop and HVAC budget retain priority
Other HVACs and tariff/15-minute PV control retain ordinary behavior
Missing room input never grants a Peak Guard exception
limitations: Battery charge direction is inferred from existing successfully published internal battery commands and the current/effective next command, not a new physical battery-power measurement.
No real Homey installation or physical battery/HVAC measurement.
The protection is transient and not restored from storage after restart.
skipped: Independent battery/phase/EV/boiler/AutoTune/planning suites; their algorithms were not changed
UI/localization regression suites; no UI strings/settings/Flows changed
